pr_title: [release/6.0-rc1] Give tvOS a special value for Personal/MyDocuments
pr_body:
Backport of #57508 to release/6.0-rc1

/cc @directhex

## Customer Impact

Fixes two issues where tvOS devices have read-only directories which are read-write on other Apple platforms; SpecialFolders.Personal (and subdirectories thereof), and TMP.

## Testing

Manual testing on Helix & local device

## Risk

Low - makes minor changes to how temp folders are calculated on all iOS-like targets, which should be more futureproof if Apple stops allowing /tmp or TMP in an OS update

Fixes #34007
Fixes #57638

Backport of https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/57508 to release/6.0-rc1

issue_context.title: Change Environment.GetFolderPath to be compatible with tvOS
issue_context.body:
As part of the mobile workloads migration, we need to ensure the apps are behaving consistently when calling into `Environment.GetFolderPath`. There is already some implementation for iOS but it looks like it's not fully compatible with existing Mono code

The second part is to ensure there is full code coverage for all `SpecialFolder` values.
comments:
We still have an important TODO that needs to be fixed for tvOS: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f48c8d581b584495079fa5f2b2789ef48546edd9/src/mono/netcore/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Environment.iOS.cs#L39-L41

Reopening to track that.

It looks like NSCachesDirectory is the preferred alternative for tvOS.

Ref: https://github.com/firebase/firebase-ios-sdk/pull/2777
Ref: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/19002
@directhex on the mono/mono version we've been using a subdirectory in `NSLibraryDirectory`: https://github.com/mono/mono/blob/main/mcs/class/corlib/System/Environment.iOS.cs#L21-L30

review_comments: Nit, but if this can't be created for some reason then Environment.GetFolderPath will throw an exception it isn't currently documented to throw.
What do you feel would be the correct approach? Don't attempt to create the folder?  Document the possible exception?

the correct thing per contract would be to eat the exception and return empty string, per API contract. 
I know it's a bit of a hassle to catch all the various possible exceptions.

if the chance of it throwing is negligible, seems fine as is.

It should only throw in the event that `NSSearchPathDirectory.NSLibraryDirectory` is readonly, the only scenario I can think of where that seems viable is a device with a 100% full disk. And that's gonna be a pretty unwell device anyway
